recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. content.content:
# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

---

## 1. Corpus MM3-H — discipline d'accès
## 3. Corpus MM23-H — raffinement

La plupart des obligations sont déjà établies par le jalon 2 ; le jalon 3 rejoue chaque cas comme exécution traduite par `simulation`.

| ID | Scénario | Attendu | Couvert (jalon 2) |
|---|---|---|---|

theorem reset_kills_blocks {k : K} {s s' : S3} {i via : Nat} (h : ResetAtStep k i via s (.ok s'))

  simp only [ResetAtPre, har, OptP] at hpre

/-- The holder is a place (A4, A5). -/
def Holder.isPlace : Holder → Bool
  | .place _ => true
  | .frame _ => false

/-- The place `p` is an owned root (A6, owned place): no parent, owned by a place. -/
def OwnedRoot (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.P[p]?) (fun pl => pl.parent = none ∧ pl.owner.isPlace = true) False

instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (OwnedRoot s p) := by
  unfold OwnedRoot; infer_instance

/-- Storage at `p` released (A6), before releasing authorities whose holder died: `p` and its
parts are dead, `p` is freed, every authority covering a leaf of `p` or held within `p` is
released, the anchors of `p` and its parts are removed. -/
def freeS (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    D := fun q => if partOf s.P q p then [] else s.D q
    dead := fun q => s.dead q || decide (partOf s.P q p)
    freed := fun q => s.freed q || decide (q = p)
    A := s.A.map fun y => if (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P p) ∨ heldIn s.P p y.holder then
      { y with active := false } else y }

/-- Effect of `free p auth` (A6): `freeS`, then the authorities whose holder died are
released. -/
def freeEff (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 := cleanup (freeS s p)

/-- Leaves whose storage ends with the release of `p` (A6): those of `p`, and those of places
that stop being usable, such as the places owned by `p`. -/
def FreedLeaf (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Prop :=
  l ∈ footprint s.P p ∨ (s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (freeS s p).Usable l)

instance (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Decidable (FreedLeaf s p l) := by
  unfold FreedLeaf; infer_instance

/-- Authority `a` is released by the release of `p` (A4, A6): it is active, and covers a leaf of
`p` or is held within `p` (released by `freeS`), or its holder is not live after `freeS`
(released by `cleanup`). Under the possession clause of `WF3`, that holder dies with `p`. -/
def FreeDeact (s : S3) (p a : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun z => z.active = true ∧ ((∃ l ∈ z.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P p) ∨
    heldIn s.P p z.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (freeS s p) z.holder)) False

instance (s : S3) (p a : Nat) : Decidable (FreeDeact s p a) := by
  unfold FreeDeact; infer_instance

/-- Authority `j` does not block the release of `p` (A6): if it is an active derived authority on
a freed leaf, or descending from an authority that the release releases (MM-03.3 §3, O3.2), it
is held within `p` or its holder dies. -/
def FreeAccessOK (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
    ((∃ l ∈ y.footprint, FreedLeaf s p l) ∨ ∃ a ∈ s.ancs j, FreeDeact s p a) →
      heldIn s.P p y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (freeS s p) y.holder) True

instance (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Decidable (FreeAccessOK s p j) := by
  unfold FreeAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Anchor `x` survives the release of `p` (A6): it covers no leaf of `p`, is not held within
`p`, and its holder stays live. -/
def FreeAnchorOK (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P p) ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P p y.holder ∧
    HolderLive (freeS s p) y.holder) True

instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (FreeAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold FreeAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `free p auth` (A6), in order: `p` deallocable by the allocator contract
(`Deallocable`) and `auth` a compatible deallocation authority (`FreeCompat`, MM-03.3.8); `p` a
usable owned root (a part is not a unit of storage, and `WF3` gives a part the `dead` flag of its
parent); exercisable `Modify` on `p` (B2); no active derived authority on a freed leaf, or
descending from a deactivated authority, held elsewhere and staying live; no usable place
anchored on an authority covering `p`, held within `p`, or whose holder dies; no freed leaf
pinned, statically (`Pinned`) or dynamically, without exception (B6: external obligations end
only through `unpin` under `ExternalDone`). -/
def FreePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) : Prop :=
  k.Deallocable p ∧ k.FreeCompat p auth ∧ s.Usable p ∧ OwnedRoot s p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, FreeAccessOK s p j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (freeS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (freeS s p).D q,
    FreeAnchorOK s p x) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, FreedLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned]
    [DecidablePred k.Deallocable] [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) :
    Decidable (FreePre k s p auth) := by
  unfold FreePre; infer_instance

/-- `free` as a relation (A6). -/
def FreeStep (k : K) (p auth : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (FreePre k s p auth) (freeEff s p)

theorem freeS_get (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : (freeS s p).A[j]? = (s.A[j]?).map fun y =>
    if (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P p) ∨ heldIn s.P p y.holder then
      { y with active := false } else y := by
  simp [freeS]

theorem freeS_releases (s : S3) (p : Nat) : OnlyReleases s (freeS s p) := by

import Ern.HandlePool

/-!

scenarios W1 to W3 of §5b. Each case is a run from the initial state `S3.init statics`

the verdict of the step under test is stated with the relation of its operation (MM-03.3 §3–6,
material §4) and decided on the reached state. The expected verdict comes from the source named in
the material, never from the module (material §0, rule 1). Every rejection has a twin: the same
run without the faulty element, where the same step is accepted (rule 2). The class (rule 5) is in
each docstring; the jalon-3 report, (a), gathers expected and obtained verdicts. Section J is not
encoded (report, (a)); `J_H42_expansion` keeps the one straight-line expansion that the kernel can
run.

Local shapes are lists of (parent, owning local, kind), as for `enterFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O6);
`lf` is a root leaf.
-/

  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

def run (statics : Statics) (os : List Op) : PS :=

import Ern.MM03.Horrors

/-!
# Measure of the `NoLock` options (jalon 3, step 4)

The options of the jalon-3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md` v2, §5), measured on the kernel as it
is (option 1, no rule), without modifying it:

* option 2, a local rule: an operation does not place an authority into a place it covers
  (`SelfLock`); `store` already rejects it (O8.3), so the rule is measured on `transfer` and
  `issue` (`opt2`);
* option 3, `NoLock`: no self-lock, as a separate clause, and the relation "`b` blocks `a`"
  (`Blocks`) acyclic, checked on the arrival state of `transfer`, `issue` and `store` (`opt3`).

For each case of the list "doit être accepté" of §5 (H11, H19, H29b, H35 to H37, H44 to H47, W1
to W3) and for H49 to H51, `decisions` gives the decision of an option on each `transfer`, `issue`
and `store` of the run of the case (`Ern.MM03.Horrors`), decided on the state where the step runs;
`true` is acceptance. The cost, measured as the brief asks (from the authorities and places the
operation touches, or the whole state): option 2 on `transfer` depends on the state only through the
places and the authorities the transfer moves (`opt2_transfer_local`), on `issue` only through the
region and the destination (`opt2_issue_local`); option 3 depends on authorities the operation does
not touch (`opt3_not_local`). Whether option 3 needs more than the function where the operation runs
(material §5, "locale à une fonction") is not settled here (report, (g)). No option is adopted (task
of jalon 3, step 4: the decision is left to arbitration).
-/

namespace Ern.MM03.LockOptions

open Ern.MM03 Ern.HandlePool Ern.MM03.Horrors

/-! ## Option 2: self-lock -/

/-- The leaves of a holder (MM-03.3.4): those of a place, none for a frame. -/
def holderLeaves (s : S3) : Holder → List Nat
  | .place p => footprint s.P p
  | .frame _ => []

/-- Self-lock of the authority `a` (material §5, options 2 and 3): `a` is active and held by a place
one of whose leaves it covers. -/
def SelfLock (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ ∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ holderLeaves s y.holder) False

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Decidable (SelfLock s a) := by unfold SelfLock; infer_instance

/-- Option 2 on `transfer src dst` (material §5): no authority moved by the transfer, one held within
the source, is self-locked in the arrival state. -/
def Opt2Transfer (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => heldIn s.P src y.holder) False →
    ¬ SelfLock (transferEff s src dst) j

instance (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Decidable (Opt2Transfer s src dst) := by
  unfold Opt2Transfer; infer_instance

/-- Option 2 on `issue` of `region` to `dst` (material §5): the block, the new authority, is not
self-locked in the arrival state. -/
def Opt2Issue (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  ¬ SelfLock (issueEff s ar region dst).1 s.A.length

instance (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (Opt2Issue s ar region dst) := by
/-- The operations checked by the options: `transfer`, `issue`, `store`. -/
def checked : Op → Bool
  | .transfer .. => true
  | .issue .. => true
  | .store .. => true
  | _ => false

/-- The decisions of the option `D` on the checked steps of a run of `K0` from `ps`, each on the
state where the step runs, in order, as long as the steps are `ok` in the kernel. -/
def decisions (D : PS → Op → Bool) (ps : PS) : List Op → List Bool
  | [] => []
  | o :: os =>
    match pexec K0 ps o with
    | some ps' => (if checked o then [D ps o] else []) ++ decisions D ps' os
    | none => []

/-- The run from `S3.init []` of a case. -/
def dec2 (os : List Op) : List Bool := decisions opt2 (PS.init []) os
def dec3 (os : List Op) : List Bool := decisions opt3 (PS.init []) os

/-! ## Cases that must be accepted (material §5) -/

/-- The runs of the cases that must be accepted, with their names: each is a run of
`Ern.MM03.Horrors` reached under `K0`, except H21's arena which is not on the list. -/
def mustAccept : List (String × List Op) :=
  [("H11", h11p ++ [.endUse 3, .endUse 6, .reset 0 0]),
   ("H19", h19p ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0 0]),
   ("H29b", h29bo), ("H35", h35o), ("H36", h36o), ("H37", h37o), ("H44", h44o),
   ("H45", h45o), ("H46", h46o), ("H47", h47o), ("W1", w1o),
   ("W2", w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19]),
   ("W3", w3o ++ [.endUse 5, .endUse 2, .endUse 3, .endUse 4, .reset 0 0, .issue 0 0 [10] 2]),
   ("W3v", w3vo ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0 0, .issue 0 0 [10] 3])]

/-- Every run of the list is `ok` in the kernel at each step, so the decisions cover all its
checked steps. -/
theorem mustAccept_runs : mustAccept.all (fun c => (prun K0 (PS.init []) c.2).isSome) = true := by
  decide

/-- The decisions of option 2 on the checked steps of each case. -/
theorem opt2_decisions : mustAccept.map (fun c => (c.1, dec2 c.2)) =
    [("H11", [true, true, true]), ("H19", [true]), ("H29b", [true]), ("H35", []),
     ("H36", []), ("H37", [true]), ("H44", [true]), ("H45", [true, true, true, true]),
     ("H46", [true]), ("H47", [true]), ("W1", []), ("W2", [true, true]),
     ("W3", [true, true, true, true, true, true, true]), ("W3v", [true, true, true, true, true, true, true])] := by
  decide

/-- The decisions of option 3 on the checked steps of each case. -/
theorem opt3_decisions : mustAccept.map (fun c => (c.1, dec3 c.2)) =
    [("H11", [true, true, true]), ("H19", [true]), ("H29b", [true]), ("H35", []),
     ("H36", []), ("H37", [true]), ("H44", [true]), ("H45", [true, true, true, true]),
     ("H46", [true]), ("H47", [true]), ("W1", []), ("W2", [true, true]),
     ("W3", [true, true, true, true, true, true, true]), ("W3v", [true, true, true, true, true, true, true])] := by
  decide

/-- No false rejection (material §5, criterion): neither option rejects a checked step of a case that
must be accepted. -/
theorem no_false_rejection : mustAccept.all (fun c => (dec2 c.2).all id && (dec3 c.2).all id) =
    true := by
  decide

/-! ## Residual blockings (H49 to H51) -/

/-- H49 (the cycle closed through a helper then its `release`): option 2 accepts every checked step,
so the blocking of H49 remains; option 3 rejects the `store` that closes the cycle (the fourth checked
step), the helper notwithstanding. -/
theorem H49_options : dec2 h49o = [true, true, true, true] ∧
    dec3 h49o = [true, true, true, false] := by
  decide

/-- The state and the step of H49 where option 3 rejects: `store 8 6` with the helper 9 active; in
its arrival state, 7 and 8 block each other. -/
theorem H49_cycle : Blocks (storeEff (run K0 [] (h48o ++ [.derive 7 6 .modify])).s 8 6) 7 8 ∧
    Blocks (storeEff (run K0 [] (h48o ++ [.derive 7 6 .modify])).s 8 6) 8 7 :=
  by decide

/-- H50 (an authority transferred or issued into the place it covers): both options reject the
`transfer` and the `issue`, by the self-lock. -/
theorem H50_options : dec2 h50ao = [true, false] ∧ dec3 h50ao = [true, false] ∧
    dec2 h50bo = [false] ∧ dec3 h50bo = [false] := by
  decide

/-- H51 (an element of a storage owned by `v` holds a view on `v`): option 2 accepts the `store`, and
would even if it checked `store`: the view is not self-locked, the configuration being a cycle of
two authorities, which option 2 does not cover (material §5); the blocking remains. Option 3 rejects
the `store`: in its arrival state, the root of the storage, held by `v`, and the view, held by the
element, block each other. -/
theorem H51_options : dec2 h51o = [true] ∧ dec3 h51o = [false] ∧
    ¬ SelfLock (storeEff (run K0 [] (h51o.take 6)).s 4 3) 4 ∧
    Blocks (storeEff (run K0 [] (h51o.take 6)).s 4 3) 2 4 ∧
    Blocks (storeEff (run K0 [] (h51o.take 6)).s 4 3) 4 2 := by
  decide

/-! ## Cost of the check -/

/-- Locality of option 2 on `transfer`: the decision depends on the state only through the places and
the authorities held within the source, the ones the transfer moves. Two states with the same places
and the same such authorities, at the same identities, get the same decision. -/
theorem opt2_transfer_local {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat} (hP : s'.P = s.P)
    (hA : ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), (s.A[j]? = some y ∨ s'.A[j]? = some y) →
      heldIn s.P src y.holder → s'.A[j]? = s.A[j]?) :
    Opt2Transfer s' src dst ↔ Opt2Transfer s src dst := by
  have key : ∀ (t t' : S3), t'.P = t.P →
      (∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), (t.A[j]? = some y ∨ t'.A[j]? = some y) →
        heldIn t.P src y.holder → t'.A[j]? = t.A[j]?) →
      Opt2Transfer t src dst → Opt2Transfer t' src dst := by
    intro t t' hP hA h j hj hheld hsl
    obtain ⟨y, hy, hh⟩ := optP_false_iff.1 hheld
    rw [hP] at hh
    have e := hA j y (.inr hy) hh
    have hy' : t.A[j]? = some y := e.symm.trans hy
    refine h j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy')) (optP_false_iff.2 ⟨y, hy', hh⟩) ?_
    have ga : (transferEff t' src dst).A[j]? = (transferEff t src dst).A[j]? := by
      rw [transfer_A_get, transfer_A_get, e, hP]
    have gl : holderLeaves (transferEff t' src dst) = holderLeaves (transferEff t src dst) := by
      funext hd

      | frame f => rfl

    exact hsl
  refine ⟨key s' s hP.symm (fun j y hy hh => ?_), key s s' hP hA⟩
  rw [hP] at hh
  exact (hA j y hy.symm hh).symm

/-- Option 2 on `issue` reads only the region and the destination: the block is self-locked exactly
when the destination's footprint meets the region. -/
theorem opt2_issue_local (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Opt2Issue s ar region dst ↔ ¬ ∃ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P dst := by
  unfold Opt2Issue SelfLock
  simp only [issueEff, S3.addAuth, List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_refl _), Nat.sub_self,
    List.getElem?_cons_zero, OptP, true_and, holderLeaves]

/-- The states of `opt3_not_local`: the state of H48 with the helper 9 (`Modify` on the node 6,
derived from 7), and the same run without the `store` of 7, which stays held by the frame. -/
def nl1 : PS := run K0 [] (h48o ++ [.derive 7 6 .modify])
def nl2 : PS := run K0 [] (fao ++ [.derive 6 6 .modify, .derive 5 5 .modify, .derive 7 6 .modify])

/-- Option 3 is not local to the operation: in two reached states where the kernel accepts

content.content:
## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage

**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.

**Options**

1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.

**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?

**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.

---

findings.claim: The W2 theorem does not prove the two claims this commit adds to its docstring. First, after system B's column authority 11 is released, "the move is accepted". Second, "one column view ... is active at the move" (A's authority 10 is released). Only `TransferStep K0 12 19 w2b.s (.ok _)` is non-vacuous. The conjunct meant to show the whole move, `PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19]))`, holds even when a step is rejected. When a step is not ok, `run` falls back to `PS.init`, and `PReach.init` reaches that state.
findings.evidence: `run` is defined as `(prun k (PS.init statics) os).getD (PS.init statics)` (Horrors.lean:32), and `PReach.init` gives `PReach k statics (PS.init statics)` (HandlePool.lean:355). The pre-commit construction is `w2oOld := w2o.dropLast`, which keeps authority 10 active. In it the move is rejected: `#eval (prun K0 (PS.init []) (w2oOld ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19])).isSome` gives `false`, and `#eval decide (TransferPre K0 w2bOld.s 9 16)` gives `false`. The W2 statement with w2o replaced by w2oOld still compiles: the first seven conjuncts close with the same proof terms, and the last with `unfold run; rw [prun … = none]; exact .init (by decide)`. `#print axioms W2_old` gives `[propext, Quot.sound]`. The same proof also closes `PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.transfer 12 19]))`, a run whose last step `W2` itself proves rejected. So the statement does not tell apart the new construction, where the move is accepted, from the old one, where it is rejected. The non-vacuous fact sits only in `LockOptions.mustAccept_runs` (isSome of the same op list), not in `W2`. Yet report (b) 3 cites `W2` for "le déplacement est accepté (`w2b`, `W2`)".
findings.fix: Replace the last conjunct with a non-vacuous one, either `(prun K0 (PS.init []) (w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19])).isSome = true` or `TransferStep K0 9 16 w2b.s (.ok (transferEff w2b.s 9 16)) ∧ TransferStep K0 12 19 (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16])).s (.ok _)`. To back the docstring's "one column view is active at the move", also add that authority 10 is inactive in `w2.s` (for example `OptP (w2.s.A[10]?) (·.active = false) False`). All of these hold by `decide`: evaluation gives authority 10 `active = false` in `w2.s`, and `TransferPre K0 w2b.s 9 16` is `true`.

The commit message says "OwnedRoot alone fails", but the theorem gives only `¬ OwnedRoot r2kt.1 5` and the rejection. It does not show that the other `FreePre` clauses hold, so it does not show that the rejection comes from `OwnedRoot` alone. The claim is true but unproved.

Second, "one column view ... is active at the move" (A's authority 10 is released). Only `TransferStep K0 12 19 w2b.s (.ok _)` is non-vacuous. The conjunct meant to show the whole move, `PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19]))`, holds even when a step is rejected. When a step is not ok, `run` falls back to `PS.init`, and `PReach.init` reaches that state.
findings.evidence: `run` is defined as `(prun k (PS.init statics) os).getD (PS.init statics)` (Horrors.lean:32), and `PReach.init` gives `PReach k statics (PS.init statics)` (HandlePool.lean:355). The pre-commit construction is `w2oOld := w2o.dropLast`, which keeps authority 10 active. In it the move is rejected: `#eval (prun K0 (PS.init []) (w2oOld ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19])).isSome` gives `false`, and `#eval decide (TransferPre K0 w2bOld.s 9 16)` gives `false`. The W2 statement with w2o replaced by w2oOld still compiles: the first seven conjuncts close with the same proof terms, and the last with `unfold run; rw [prun … = none]; exact .init (by decide)`. `#print axioms W2_old` gives `[propext, Quot.sound]`. The same proof also closes `PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.transfer 12 19]))`, a run whose last step `W2` itself proves rejected. So the statement does not tell apart the new construction, where the move is accepted, from the old one, where it is rejected. The non-vacuous fact sits only in `LockOptions.mustAccept_runs` (isSome of the same op list), not in `W2`. Yet report (b) 3 cites `W2` for "le déplacement est accepté (`w2b`, `W2`)".
findings.fix: Replace the last conjunct with a non-vacuous one, either `(prun K0 (PS.init []) (w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19])).isSome = true` or `TransferStep K0 9 16 w2b.s (.ok (transferEff w2b.s 9 16)) ∧ TransferStep K0 12 19 (run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .transfer 9 16])).s (.ok _)`. To back the docstring's "one column view is active at the move", also add that authority 10 is inactive in `w2.s` (for example `OptP (w2.s.A[10]?) (·.active = false) False`). All of these hold by `decide`: evaluation gives authority 10 `active = false` in `w2.s`, and `TransferPre K0 w2b.s 9 16` is `true`.

findings.claim: The docstring's new claim "the block value ended, so the other clauses of `free` hold" is not in the statement. The commit message says "OwnedRoot alone fails", but the theorem gives only `¬ OwnedRoot r2kt.1 5` and the rejection. It does not show that the other `FreePre` clauses hold, so it does not show that the rejection comes from `OwnedRoot` alone. The claim is true but unproved.
findings.evidence: `FreePre` (MM03.lean:4159) has the clauses `Deallocable ∧ FreeCompat ∧ Usable ∧ OwnedRoot ∧ HasRight .modify ∧ ∀ j, FreeAccessOK ∧ anchor clause ∧ pin clause`. The statement of `H06` includes only `K2f.Deallocable 5`, `K2f.FreeCompat 5 7` and `¬ OwnedRoot r2kt.1 5`. Evaluated in a scratch file, `decide (r2kt.1.Usable 5)`, `decide (HasRight r2kt.1 .modify 5)`, `decide (∀ j ∈ List.range r2kt.1.A.length, FreeAccessOK r2kt.1 5 j)`, the `FreeAnchorOK` clause and the pin clause (with `K2f.Pinned`) all give `true`. So the claim holds, but only by evaluation outside the theorem.
findings.fix: Add the remaining clauses as conjuncts of `H06`, each closed by `by decide`: `r2kt.1.Usable 5 ∧ HasRight r2kt.1 .modify 5 ∧ (∀ j ∈ List.range r2kt.1.A.length, FreeAccessOK r2kt.1 5 j) ∧ …`. Otherwise, remove the claim from the docstring.
